(VOTE TAKEN) 37 Webb Street (AP 52 Lot 555) Amit Anand seeks preliminary plan approval for a major amendment to the approved plan for a two-family dwelling on a 4000 +/- sqft tract of land, owned by Amit and Marissa Anand, zoned Residential Multifamily (RM) fronting on Webb Street, identified as Assessor’s Plat 52, Lot 555, and addressed as 37 Webb. The applicant requests a major amendment in order to construct an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) within an under-construction two-family residential structure with four par king spaces. The project will require the review of a variance for minimum parking for an ADU under § 410-46(B)(4)(c) of the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance. Staff presented Amit Anand's request for a major amendment to add an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) within an approved two-family structure. The project was previously granted final plan approval and now returns for amendment to reconfigure the internal structure to add an ADU. Staff explained that the applicant requests relief from the requirement of one off-street parking space per ADU, proposing zero additional parking spaces for the ADU, but maintaining four total spaces for the site. Staff noted that the applicant requested a parking variance rather than a front-yard paving variance, which staff found more beneficial to the public welfare. Commissioner Bruggemann clarified for the record that under state law, ADUs are not considered additional units for zoning purposes. Amit Anand, the applicant, confirmed that the ADU would be located on the first flo or behind the garage parking spaces. All Planning Commission meetings are open meetings unless otherwise stated. PICOZZI, MAYOR City of Warwick Approved Planning Board Meeting Minutes June 10, 2026 Members Present: Philip Slocum, Chairman Kevin Flynn, Vice-Chair Tammy Bouchard-Baker Steven Catalano Justin Mateus Members Absent: Linda Polselli Benny Bergantino Kyla Pecchia Ashley Cullion Also in Attendance: Thomas Kravitz, Director/Administrative Officer Ashley Smith, Planning Assistant David Petrarca, Solicitor Chairman Phil Slocum called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. Meeting Minutes On the motion of Kevin Flynn, seconded by Steven Catalano the Board voted to approve the May Minutes. All Members in Favor. Steve Catalano motioned to open the meeting to the public, seconded by Tammy Bouchard Baker. Applications 445 Palmer Ave This application will be heard before the board at the August 12th Planning Board Meeting. Motion for continuance was put forth by chairman Philip Slocum, seconded by Kevin Flynn. All members were in favor. Centerville & Legris This application to construct 14 new condominium units was required to come before the board for Final approval to ensure stormwater drainage was satisfactory to the City’s standards. The DPW found the amended plans to be satisfactory and are comfortable going forward. There were no comments from the public and a motion to authorize the Director to render and record a positive, Final decision of approval was motioned by Kevin Flynn, seconded by Steven Catalano. All members were in favor. PLANNING DEPARTMENT ● THOMAS KRAVITZ, DIRECTOR 3275 POST ROAD ● WARWICK, RI 02886 ● 401-738-2009 Pre-Application for 192 Tollgate Rd. A potential PDR application for 10 units consisting of two four-unit buildings and one two-unit building was presented to the Board as a pre-application. The lot is quite narrow and subject to development constraints and steep slopes on the western 1/3 of the property. Significant dimensional relief would be required as every building is roughly 8/10ths outside of the building setback envelope. Residential uses are limited in the area due to a higher concentration of Office uses that compliment the medical industry. The Comprehensive Plan supports the expansion of medical uses along this section of Toll Gate Road, and for these reasons, the applicant was discouraged from advancing the project. Subdividing the property off to neighbors and or considering a smaller modest office with several parking spaces was suggested by the Board. Pre Application for 2 Shattock Ave The Board provided positive feedback on the pre-application to construct a private clubhouse at the marina. It was not viewed as egregious with respect to size or height and the architecture was in keeping with what one would expect to see at a marina in New England. A more robust discussion occurred around the private litigation that is occurring amongst title companies involving the applicant and the neighbor at 99 Midgley Avenue. As confirmed by the applicants’ attorney Mr. Landry, there is litigation revolving around the subject of access for 99 Midgley which historically was allowed through the Marina – a right that has apparently been terminated. The Planning Director presented what he surmised to be a questionable administrative subdivision plan masking as a boundary survey recorded as, MAP # 621. The map, not signed by City staff, was recorded on September 2, 2021 at 1:06 p.m. by an unknown party with the transaction being paid for in cash. Earlier that same day at approximately 10:42 a.m., abutting property 99 Midgley Ave (Plat 365, Lot 157) was transacted from Barbara A. Durrell-Dickerson to Danelle M. Debye. And while the applicant’s attorney, Mr. Landry, positioned the notion of access with a neighbor to be a mutually exclusive title issue to the application before the Board, the Board felt hesitant about approving further development of the marina that may preclude proper resolution or remedy to the existing litigation. Mr. Landy agreed to bring the new information to his client, which may inform and bring closure to the private, ongoing lawsuit, and provide an update to the Board along with the Preliminary

Case no. 24-069MA – 70 Houghton Street Applicant: College Hill Development LLC Owner: Providence Redevelopment Agency The applicant is proposing to construct seven commercial multi-purpose buildings with associated improvements on the vacant subject lot in the M-MU 75 zone. The applicant is requesting preliminary plan approval and is seeking a waiver from submission of the site survey – for vote (AP 78 Lot 457, Wanskuck) Mr. Manjrekar introduced the item. Engineer Brandon Carr presented the plan on behalf of the applicant. He said a waiver from submission of the site survey was requested given on-site surveying difficulties as a long-undeveloped site. Mr. Azar said that the land had been owned by the Providence Redevelopment Agency for many years, with no notable development plans created during that time. The project will include seven warehouse buildings built on an approximately nine-acre area, with three stormwater catchment basins and a landscaped tree buffer. The warehouses will likely not have a high traffic volume from large trucks. A discussion of warehouse use ensued, clarifying that the warehouses would be used for interior storage, but not for distribution or exterior storage. Mr. Manjrekar read out the DPD's staff report which found the project to be in conformance with the zoning ordinance and comprehensive plan. He recommended that the CPC grant the waiver and approve the preliminary plan. Mr. Gazdacko said the project would be economically beneficial to the area. Action – Waiver On a motion by Commissioner McKenna, seconded by Commissioner Sanchez, the CPC voted to grant the waiver from submission of a survey finding that it would be in the interest of good planning practice and subject to the following condition: The applicant shall submit the survey with the final plan submission. The CPC voted as follows: Aye: C. McKenna, N. Sanchez, R. Dotson, M. Gazdacko Action – Preliminary Plan On a motion by Commissioner Sanchez seconded by Commissioner Dotson, the CPC voted to approve the preliminary plan, finding that the project was in conformance with the zoning ordinance and comprehensive plan and subject to the following condition: The drainage plan shall be subject to the City Engineer's approval. The CPC voted as follows: Aye: N. Sanchez, R. Dotson, C. McKenna, M. Gazdacko MAJOR LAND DEVELOPMENT PROJECT PUBLIC HEARING 4. Case no. 26-046UDR – 14 Cargill Street Applicant and Owner: Rhode Island Public Health Institute The applicant is proposing to construct of a four story, approximately 52' tall medical services building with associated site amenities. The applicant is requesting a design waiver from the build to percentage on West Street and a dimensional variance from the parking requirement. The applicant has requested waivers from submission of a lighting plan and submission of state approvals at the preliminary plan stage. The applicant is requesting to combine master and preliminary plan approval – for vote (AP 29 Lots 108 and 550, Federal Hill) – (A transcript for this item is available upon request and has been made part of the record) Mr. Manjrekar introduced the item. Attorney Joseph Shekarchi represented the applicant and introduced the plan on behalf of the applicant. Architect Jackie Brousseau, Engineer Christine Shea, Traffic Engineer Philip Fusco and Amy Nunn, CEO of the Rhode Island Public Health Institute also spoke on the applicant's behalf. A discussion on the item ensued with the CPC hearing from the applicant, their experts and taking public comment. On a motion by Commissioner Sanchez, seconded by Commissioner Dotson, the CPC voted to approve the design waiver from the build-to percentage on West Street. The CPC voted as follows: Aye: N. Sanchez, R. Dotson, C. McKenna, M. Gazdacko Commissioner Sanchez made a motion, seconded by Commissioner McKenna, to approve the dimensional variance from the parking requirement. The CPC voted as follows: Aye: N. Sanchez, M. Gazdacko Nay: C. McKenna, R. Dotson The motion did not pass as it did not receive a majority of favorable votes. Ms. Disanto said it was unclear if the CPC's action amounted to a denial or a vote of no action. She said additional time was needed to research the action and how it would affect the approval of the master and preliminary plan. A discussion on the review process ensued. On a motion by Commissioner Sanchez, seconded by Commissioner McKenna, the CPC voted to continue the item to the August 18th meeting. The CPC voted as follows: Aye: N. Sanchez, C. McKenna, R. Dotson, M. Gazdacko Adjournment On a motion by Commissioner Sanchez, seconded by Commissioner Dotson, the CPC voted to adjourn the meeting at 7:59 pm. All voted in favor. The subject property and the surrounding area are primarily residential in nature and the request does not propose or encourage incompatible uses that would be disruptive to the surrounding area. The Board further found the following: • The residences surrounding 309 Station Street are historic remnants of the Auburn neighborhood that were separated from it by the construction of I-95. • 1965 Zoning Plats show that this sliver of land wedged between the railroad and the highway, is made up of mostly two-family homes. o The subject property was previously designated as a two-family dwelling. • The applicant is not proposing any significant changes to the lot or the structure. Existing lot size and frontage are in excess of requirements for two -family dwellings in zones where they are permitted. Applying the M -2 zoning requirements would be inconsistent with the surrounding neighborhood and the historic use of the lot. • The Future Land Use Map acknowledges that this industrial zone should be changed to allow for redevelopment. This area may be suitable for industrial uses, but the existing residential buildings are here to stay. Continuing the residential use will not interfere with current or future industrial operations in the area. In this case, the Board voted to accept the staff finding of fact and applying the facts above to the standard for a variance, the Board further finds that the application involves a hardship that is not due to a physical or economic disability of the appl icant, and the applicant would suffer more than a mere inconvenience if the variance were denied. The relief sought is minimal to a reasonable enjoyment of the permitted use to which the property is proposed to be devoted and will not alter the general character of the surrounding area or impair the intent or purpose of the Zoning Ordinance or the comprehensive plan. In granting a variance the Applicant met the requirements of the Zoning Code and relief per 17.92.010- Variance; Section 17.20.030 Schedule of Uses; Section 17.20.120 Schedule of Intensity Regulations. Doorley, Jr. Municipal Building, 444 Westminster Street, Providence, RI 02903. DRC Application No. 18.38: 187-203 Westminster Street (Old Providence Journal Building and Kresge Building ) Proposal by Westminster Partners, LLC to convert both buildings into a new hotel. Work includes construction of a new rooftop penthouse, restoration of building facades, and installation of new storefronts, canopies and signage. Eric Zuena, Julie Bartlett, and Steven Wolenski, from ZDS, Inc., and Jim Abdo, developer, appeared to discuss the project. Mr. Abdo gave a brief and enthusiastic introduction. Mr. Zuena gave a project overview, noting that there is a façade easement on the Providence Journal Building, and that the Rhode Island Historic Preservation Commission (RIHPC) is in the process of reviewing the project. A letter from the RIHPC was submitted. He added that the project will be a hotel with a mixed-use environment. Mr. Zuena stated that the 77,000-sf Providence Journal Building will contain 91 guestrooms and the 42,000-sf Kresge Building will contain 48 guestrooms. He noted that they are proposing to enlarge the penthouse on the roof of the Providence Journal Building. Ms. Bartlett made a PowerPoint presentation regarding the proposed building alterations. Regarding the alterations to the Providence Journal Building, she explained that a non- original chimney is to be removed, new canopies installed, new wall signage installed (based on historic photos), illumination of the façade, and a reintroduction of the Westminster Street entrance with a new canopy. Ms. Bartlett presented floor plans, roof plan, and elevations. She stated that new skylights for new guestrooms on the top floor are proposed in the flat part of the roof and will not be visible from the street. Mr. Zuena explained that the new canopies proposed over the Eddy and Fulton Street entrances will have glass roofs for vertical visibility. Ms. Bartlett explained that a few existing storefronts are to be replaced with operable windows. Mr. Ise noted a couple of issues regarding the proposed storefront modifications and exterior cladding for the penthouse. Doorley, Jr. Municipal Building, 444 Westminster Street, Providence, RI 02903. OPENING SESSION Members Present: Kristi Gelnett, Clark Schoettle, Libby Isaacson, Shey Rivera, and Rachel Hampton Members Absent: Chris Marsella and Alan Chille Staff Present: Christopher Ise, Robert Azar, and Lisa Dinerman, Legal Counsel Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 4:55 pm, Ms. Gelnett, Chair, presiding. Meeting Minutes of March 11, 2019: Ms. Isaacson made a motion, seconded by Mr. Schoettle, to approve the meeting minutes. All voted in favor. NEW BUSINESS 1. DRC Application No. 19.05: 10 Orms Street – Public Hearing The subject of the hearing was an application by First Circle Realty, LLC, requesting a waiver from Zoning Ordinance Section 1604.G, Illumination Standards, which prohibits internally illuminated face- lit signs in the D-1 Zone. The applicant is seeking to install three (3) new internally illuminated face-lit wall signs on the building located at 10 Orms Street, Providence, RI. Colin Kane and Jeff carter, from Dion Signs, appeared to discuss the project. Mr. Kane explained that First Circle Realty acquired the property, noting that Delta Dental will occupy the building. He explained that the objective is to upgrade the common areas of the building, integrate the parking lots with the adjacent Delta Dental Building, and improve the landscaping. Mr. Kane stated that the plan is to brand the building ‘Chewsi Center,’ which is a retail dental product. Mr. Carter presented two illuminated letter samples, one showing a halo-lit letter, and the other the showing a face-lit letter. Mr. Carter explained that the ‘Chewsi’ sign will have face-lit letters and the ‘Center’ sign will be halo-lit. There was no public comment. The public hearing was closed. Mr. Schoettle made a motion, seconded by Ms. Isaacson to grant the requested waiver and final design approval, based on the findings of fact and recommendations in the staff report. Members Gelnett, Schoettle, Isaacson, Rivera, and Hampton voted in favor. Ms. Isaacson recused herself from the following discussion. 2. DRC Application No. 19.07: 250 Dyer Street (Portion of I-195 Redevelopment District Parcel 42) Proposal by Fane Tower, LLC to construct a new 46-story building, consisting of residential units, structured parking, and ground floor retail. The applicant is seeking waivers, per Providence Zoning Ordnance Section 1601.D, from Sections 606. A.2, Building height and massing, 606.D.1, Building facades built within a build-to-zone, 606.D.2, Building facade transition line, and 606.E.3, Upper story facade transparency. At this meeting, the DDRC conceptually reviewed the project and made a recommendation to the I-195 Redevelopment District Commission regarding the building design and waivers. William Landry, attorney, and Gianni Ria, architect, appeared to present the project. Mr. Landry noted that certain portions of the staff report potentially raise legal interpretative issues as to when design review ceases to be design review and becomes something else. He explained that two of the requested waivers deal with whether the proposed design relates to adjoining buildings . He went on to say that the staff report recommends against those waivers because a building this tall could never relate to surrounding buildings. Mr. Landry stated that their position is that the City Council created a subdistrict of height (up to 600’) that advanced several important objectives in the Comprehensive Plan. Mr. Landry DDRC Meeting Minutes – 4/8/19 2 stated that the interpretation should be whether or not the applicant has made the proposed building relate to the surrounding buildings. He suggested that the starting point should be reviewing a building that is up to 600’ tall. Mr. Ria gave a powerpoint presentation on the design of the new tower , explaining the site layout, podium design, and the tower. Regarding the ground floor of the podium, Mr. Ria noted that they have addressed concerns by extending the retail portion to the east, and maximizing the frontages to create a pedestrian friendly environment along the perimeter. OPENING SESSION Members Present: Kristi Gelnett, Clark Schoettle , Libby Isaacson, Shey Rivera, and Rachel Hampton Members Absent : Chris Marsella and Alan Chille Staff Present: Christopher Ise, Robert Azar, and Lisa Dinerman, Legal Counsel Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 4:55 pm, Ms. Gelnett, Chair, presiding. Meeting Minutes of March 11, 2019: Ms. Isaacson made a motion, seconded by Mr. Schoettle, to approve the meeting minutes. All voted in favor. NEW BUSINESS 1. DRC Application No. 19.05: 10 Orms Street – Public Hearing The subject of the hearing was an application by First Circle Realty, LLC, requesting a waiver from Zoning Ordinance Section 1604.G, Illumination Standards, which prohibits internally illuminated face -lit signs in the D-1 Zone. The applicant is seeking to install three (3) new internal ly illuminated face -lit wall signs on the building located at 10 Orms Street, Providence, RI. Colin Kane and Jeff carter, f rom Dion Signs, appeared to discuss the project. Mr. Kane explained that First Circle Realty acquired the property, noting that Delt a Dental will occupy the building. He explained that the objective is to upgrade the common areas of the building, integrate the parking lots with the adjacent Delta Dental Building, and improve the landscaping. Mr. Kane stated that the plan is to brand the building ‘Chewsi Center,’ which is a retail dental product. Mr. Carter presented two illuminated letter samples, one showing a halo-lit letter , and the other the showing a face -lit letter . Mr. Carter explained that the ‘Chewsi’ sign will have face -lit le tters and the ‘Center’ sign will be halo -lit. There was no public comment. The public hearing was closed. Mr. Schoettle made a motion, seconded by Ms. Isaacson to grant the requested waiver and final design approval, based on the findings of fact and r ecommendations in the staff report. Members Gelnett, Schoettle, Isaacson, Rivera, and Hampton voted in favor. Ms. Isaacson recused herself f rom the following discussion. 2. DRC Application No. 19.07: 250 Dyer Street (Portion of I -195 Redevelopment District Parcel 42) Proposal by Fane Tower, LLC to construct a new 46 -story building, consisting of residential units, structured parking, and ground floor retail. The applicant is seeking waivers, per Providence Zoning Ordnance Section 1601.D, from Sections 606. A.2, Building height and massing , 606.D.1, Building facades built within a build -to-zone, 606.D.2, Building facade transition line , and 606.E.3, Upper story facade transparency. At this meeting, the DDRC conceptually reviewed the project and made a recommendation to the I -195 Redevelopment District Commission regarding the building design and waivers. William Landry, attorney, and Gian ni Ria, architect, appeared to present the project. Mr. Landry noted that certain portions of the staff report potentially raise legal interpretative issues as to when design review ceases to be design review and becomes something else. He explained that two of the requested waivers deal with whether the proposed de sign relates to adjoining buildings . He went on to say that the staff report recommends against those waivers because a building this tall could never relate to surrounding buildings. Mr. Landry stated that their position is that the City Council created a subdistrict of height (up to 600’) that advanced several important objectives in the Comprehensive Plan. Mr. Landry DDRC Meeting Minutes – 4/8/19 2 stated that the interpretation should be whether or not the applicant has made the proposed building relate to the surrounding buildings. H e suggested that the starting point should be reviewing a building that is up to 600’ tall. Mr. Ria gave a powerpoint presentation on the design of the new tower , explaining the site layout, podium design, and the tower. Regarding the ground floor of the podium, Mr. Ria noted that they have addressed concerns by extending the retail portion to the east, and maximizing the frontages to create a pedestrian friendly environment along the perimeter. He went on to say that the back of the house operations, a n ecessity, will be at the end of Dorrance Street. The elevator core will have two main access points and lobbies for residential entrances. Elevators will have a high -rise and low-rise component. He mentioned that the podium has been set back at the corner of Dyer and Dorrance Streets to create an open plaza for activation. Mr. Ria presented a typical parking level. He noted that due to the pie shaped site, the parking layout is not efficient; however it has been configured to

rials. Mr. Herlong explained that the sign is constructed of steel and aluminum, in a matte finish, with laser cut letters in the metal panel, noting that the letters will be illuminated and not the face of the sign. In response to a question by Mr. Schoettle, Mr. Herlong replied that it is possible that future buildings may have pylon signs. The consensus among the members was that the sign looks good. Mr. Schoettle made a motion, seconded by Ms. Isaacson, to make a recommendation to the I -195 Redevelopment District Commission to grant the waiver, and to approve the sign as designed. All voted in favor. 2. DRC Application No. 19.03: 2 Kennedy Plaza (Alex and Ani City Center) Proposal by the City of Providence to alter the existing roof of the City Center Building by removing the center viewing porch and roof. Bonnie Nickerson, Planning Director, and Glen Fontecchio, architect, appeared to present the project. A powerpoint presentation as made. Ms. Nickerson explained that the building is a gateway, but also a visual barrier into the rink and beyond to Union Station. She presented the Greater Kennedy Plaza Vision Plan, noting that the initial plan was to remove the building in its entirety; however, the Parks Department wants to keep the existing businesses in the building. The plan now calls for the partial removal of the existing roof over the three center bays and its support columns. She explained that the reason for the removal of the center portion is due to the new Downtown Transit Circulator shelter which is to be located in the East Approach roadway. The roadway, which now currently provides vehicular and truck access into the rink (for events), is to be permanently closed. She added that the other structures proposed for the park would be reviewed by the DDRC.Ms. Gelnett commented that it would be nice to open the views into the rink. Mr. Fontecchio briefly explained the removal of the roof and repair to the building, with all work to match existing. Mr. Chille made a motion, seconded by Mr. Schoettle, to DDRC Meeting Minutes – 3/11/19 2 approve the application, citing DRC Standard 9 and the findings of fact in the staff report. All voted in favor. At this time, Ms. Dinerman recommended reopening DDRC application 19.02, 225 Dyer Street. Ms. Isaacson made a motion, seconded by Mr. Chille, to reopen the application. All voted in favor. The findings of fact for the waiver, and the staff’s findings of fact were read into the record. OTHER BUSINESS Pre-Application Review 3. Proposed Residential Tower at 250 Dyer Street (Portion of I-195 Redevelopment District Parcel 42) Proposal by The Fane Organization to construct a new 46-story building, consisting of approximately 448 residential units, structured parking, and ground floor retail. This item was for discussion only. No action was taken by the DDRC at the meeting, nor was public comment taken. Mr. Azar explained that the Providence City Council approved a zoning change for the subject land from D1-100 to D1-600 in December 2018, adding that the Council also amended some text in Article 6 of the Zoning Ordinance related to waivers. He explained that the DRC can now grant waivers for the requirement that building height and massing relate to adjacent structures, and the requirement that a building façade have a transition line. Mr. Azar stated that DDRC would review thi s project on advisory level, however for this meeting the applicant was giving an informal presentation to the DDRC with no action to be taken. He added that there are two further stages of review, conceptual and final design review, where public comment will be taken. Jeff Padwa, attorney, and Gianni Ria, architect, appeared to present the project. Mr. Padwa gave a brief overview, noting several meetings with Planning staff. Mr. Ria gave a powerpoint presentation. He focused on the podium and the pedestrian level, noting the ‘Flatiron Building’ shape at the corner of Dorrance and Dyer Street, and its potential to be an iconic building. He went on to explain that the retail spaces and building lobby will be along major streets, with building services at the rear. Regarding the tower floor plans, he explained that the lower floors will have smaller units, increasing to large size units at top floors. Mr. Ria presented podium design Option A, which reflects the design of the adjacent Wexford Building, with a 3-dimensional quality and colonnade. Exterior materials include metal, glass, and stone elements. Mr. Ria then presented podium design Option B , noting that he changed the building’s vocabulary. He explained that Option B looks more like an office build ing, adding that he preferred Option A, which he considers a superior design. Ms. Gelnett asked for comments by the DRC members. Mr. Schoettle stated that he has an issue with the building’s massing and suggested reducing the scale and height to make it more compatible with the surrounding buildings. A motion was made by Everett O’Donnell, seconded by Paul DePetrillo and passed unanimously by the Board that Mr. Cabral be accepted as an expert witness. Mr. Cabral state the subject property is a unique size & shape. There is a historical cemetery in the back of the building. They will not be increasing the non-conformity. They will be reconfiguring the parking area to add parking in the front. Mr Shekarchi stated they are improving what is there. This is a national brand. The petitioners area making a large investment in upgrades, and is a good use in a great location. The Chairman asked if there was anyone present in opposition or in favor of the petition. There being none, Everett O’Donnell stated the property has been vacant, and it will be a good use for the City of Warwick, and made a motion to approve the petition, seconded by Julie Finn and passed unanimously by the Board that the petition be GRANTED

Petition #10616 Ward 5 30 Randall Ave. The petition of Frank & Sheryl Williams, 30 Randall Ave., Warwick, RI, requests a dimensional variance to convert the existing detached garage to an accessory dwelling unit on the existing undersized non-conforming lot. Proposed accessory dwelling having less than required rear yard setback, having a separate entrance, and larger than allowed by Ordinance. Assessor’s Plat 378, Lot 85, zoned Residential A-40. Mary Shekarchi, Esq. was present and representing the petitioners. Daniel Geagan from the Planning Department read the recommendations into the record. Ms. Shekarchi stated the proposal is to convert the existing detached garage into an ac- cessory dwelling unit for Mr. Williams’s elderly mother. She stated this will conform to the law recently passed by State, RIGL 45-24-37, in which recognizes accessory dwelling units for family members with disabilities or over the age of 62 years old. Ms. Shekarchi stated the main dwelling has three bedrooms, but Mr. Williams’s mother has trouble with her legs, so it would be beneficial to have her live in a one story struc- ture. The existing garage doors will remain, as to not change the appearance of the structure. The petitioner agreed to the stipulations placed on the approval by the Planning Department, and to record a “Declaration of Restrictions” with the decision letter in the Land Evidence Records of the City Clerk’s Office. The relief being sought is for the rear yard setback. The required setback is 20’, and the existing structure has a rear setback of 9.6’. All other setbacks will be met. There were many neighbors present in objection of the petition. They had concerns with the subject property not meeting the requirements for an accessory dwelling unit and should be part of the principal residential structure, and not a stand-alone structure. They feel this is a second dwelling unit that may be rented to non-family members in the future. Everett O’Donnell stated he grew up on that street and most of those houses were summer cottages on small lots. Since the house was constructed in 1835, the zoning re- quirements have changed over the years. They have a right to ask to expand. Peter Clarkin, the City Solicitor stated this is for a unique situation for accessory dwelling units. He read RIGL 45-24-37 and stated this law takes precedents over the Zoning Ordinance. It’s for a family member with a disability or over the age of 62 years old, it will cease once the family member passes away or the property is transferred to a new

DRC Application No. 19.37: 91 Clemence Street (commercial building) Proposal by AS220 to install a permanent mural on the north elevation of the building. 2. DRC Application No. 19.36: 151-155 Chestnut Street – Public Hearing and Conceptual Design Review The subject of the hearing will be an application by Providence Chestnut 1, LLC, to demolish the existing structures located at 151 Chestnut Street and 155 Chestnut Street, and to construct a new 12 -story, mixed-use building at 151-155 Chestnut Street. The applicant is requesting a Downtown District Demolition Waiver (Zoning Ordinance Section 1907.2). The applicant is also requesting a developm ent incentive in the form of a 30% height bonus (Zoning Ordinance Section 1907.E.2.f), and waivers from Zoning Ordinance Sections 606.A.4, Building Height and Massing/ Recess Line, and 606.E.1 Building Facades/Ground Floor Transparency. At the conclusion of the hearing, the DDRC will take action with respect to these items. OLD BUSINESS 3. DRC Application No. 17.05: 229 Dyer Street, Proposed Aloft Hotel Sign (I-195 Redevelopment District Parcel 22) Proposal by Providence Innovation District Phase I Owner, LLC (owner) and BAC CVP Aloft LLC (applicant), to install an internally illuminated projecting sign on the façade of the proposed hotel building. The applicant is requesting waivers from Providence Zoning Ordinance Section 1604.G, for a type of internal illumination for the sign that is prohibited in the D-1 Zone, and Section 1607.H, for a projecting sign that exceeds the maximum sign area allowed in the D-1 Zone. The DDRC will review the project and make a recommendation to the I-195 Redevelopment District Commission regarding the sign design and requested waivers. (over) 4. DRC Application No. 19.25: 135 Wickenden Street (I-195 Redevelopment District Parcel 6) East Side I-195 Overlay District Continued review of the proposal by D+P Real Estate and Truth Box Inc. to construct a mixed-use development on the property, consisting of a grocery store, 62 dwelling units, and other commercial space. The applicant will also be seeking a Development Incentive in the form of a height bonus (Section 1103.F.2) for one additional story on the building fronting South Water Street. The DDRC will review the project and make a final recommendation to the I-195 Redevelopment District Commission regarding the development incentive and building design. 5. DRC Application No. 19.32: 125 Clifford Street (I-195 Redevelopment District Parcel 28) Continued review of the proposal by EM 28 Providence, LLC to construct a new building consisting of 248 residential units, ground floor retail, and on-site parking. The DDRC will review the project and make a final recommendation to the I-195 Redevelopment District Commission regarding the building design. Referral 3479 – 50 Ashburton Street Petitioners: Goulding Properties and EJS Investments Inc The petitioner is requesting to rezone 50 Ashburton Street from M-1 to M-MU 75 – for action (AP 2 Lot 15, Smith Hill) Mr. Potter returned to the meeting. Mr. Manjrekar introduced the item. Mr. John Garrahy represented the applicant. He said the purpose of the rezoning was to allow for conversion of the former industrial building to a multifamily dwelling. The property is under the jobs district of the comprehensive plan. He asked that the CPC make a positive recommendation for the zone change with the comprehensive plan change to come later. Mr. Azar shared a map of the future land use map of the comprehensive plan to explain the effect of the jobs district. He said the comprehensive plan change could be heard at a future meeting so that the zoning and comprehensive plan change could occur simultaneously. A discussion on the changes ensued. Mr. Potter said there was little industrial activity in proximity to the site and the jobs district designation was not appropriate. Mr. Gazdacko said the building had remained vacant for a long time and it would be appropriate to have active use on the site. Ms. Salvatore said a zone change occurring before a comprehensive plan change was not customary but could occur if both were made to conform in proximity to each other. A discussion on the change ensued. Mr. Manjrekar read out the DPD’s staff report which recommended that the zone change be approved with the comprehensive plan occurring in proximity to the change. Upon a motion by Commissioner Gazdacko, seconded by Commissioner Quezada, the CPC unanimously voted to recommend that the City Council approve the proposed zone change based on their findings. In accordance with their action, the CPC recommended that the zone change be approved. The CPC advised that the comprehensive plan’s Future Land Use Map should eventually be changed to clarify the limits of the Jobs District. The CPC voted as follows: AYE: M. Gazdacko, M. Quezada, C.
